articles.title: RFK Jr. vows to curb a measles crisis he initially underestimated
articles.summary: Hours after the United States lost its measles-elimination status, erasing a landmark public health victory earned 26 years ago, Health Secretary Robert F. K...
articles.body:
Hours after the United States lost its measles-elimination status, erasing a landmark public health victory earned 26 years ago, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declared the country would fight the spread of the disease.

"We will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status," Kennedy posted on X. "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles."

But as federal and state governments confront the spread of one of the world's most contagious diseases, some state and local officials question whether Kennedy and his department can bring it under control. Kennedy had sowed doubt about the safety of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine for years and, as the top U.S. health official, has sought major changes to childhood immunization policy, to cheers from some supporters of his Make America Healthy Again movement. Those actions, some public health experts say, have complicated efforts to persuade more Americans to get vaccinated and rebuild the population immunity needed to bring outbreaks under control.

As federal health agencies deployed resources to West Texas in 2025, Kennedy initially underestimated the resurgence of the disease, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe internal matters.

"It took him a while to accept measles as something that wasn't going to go away quickly," said a former health official.

Federal health officials must now develop a corrective action plan for the Pan American Health Organization, the regional health agency that withdrew the U.S.'s measles elimination status, outlining how the country will stop continuous spread of the virus and regain its status. PAHO officials said they expect the plan in the coming weeks, although there is no formal deadline.

Even before the U.S. officially lost its designation, federal officials began taking steps toward that effort. Erica Schwartz, the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, met earlier this month with public health groups to discuss strategies for curbing the outbreaks and to identify challenges, according to two public health officials with knowledge of the meeting who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe private conversations.

The CDC, state health officials, epidemiologists and national immunization groups are also planning regional meetings to coordinate the response, with special attention to improving outreach to vulnerable communities.

The Department of Health and Human Services said it has been aggressive in fighting measles. Since August, the CDC has made $100 million available to states to improve the response. It has provided help from CDC scientists to states battling outbreaks, including Texas, South Carolina, New York, Wisconsin and Pennsylvania.

"We will address PAHO's findings directly," HHS spokeswoman Emily Hilliard said in a statement. "HHS and CDC will address the findings and work with partners to document interruption of endemic transmission and meet the requirements for re-achieving elimination status."

State and local health officials say they welcome those efforts. But stopping continuous spread of the virus requires a broader and sustained effort, including raising vaccination rates in communities where coverage has fallen before Kennedy came into office. Only the federal government can do what states cannot do on their own, such as coordinate across states, bring health and immunization officials together, and provide robust funding and expertise.

New York's health commissioner, James McDonald, said at a briefing Thursday with reporters that PAHO's decision was expected well in advance, and a federal plan should have already been prepared.

"I'm already concerned that Health and Human Services does not have a national plan," McDonald said. New York, which declared a state disaster emergency in response to its outbreak, recorded a measles-related child death - its first in over 30 years - earlier this month.

Others say losing elimination status should itself prompt a strong response across all levels of government.

"I do hope it's a wake-up call for CDC, for Congress, for HHS, for everyone," said Claire Hannan, the executive director of the Association of Immunization Managers. "We need to be doing more."

As the founder of a prominent anti-vaccine group, Kennedy had for years raised questions about the safety of the MMR vaccine. He previously linked the shot to autism despite decades of contradictory evidence. And he wrote in a book that measles outbreaks have been "fabricated" to "inflict unnecessary and risky vaccines" on millions of children.

As the West Texas outbreak grew in early 2025, Kennedy coupled messages encouraging vaccination with false or misleading claims about the MMR vaccine. He promoted alternative treatments and questioned whether a child who state health officials said died of measles had actually died of the disease.

His claims that vaccines contain "aborted fetus debris and DNA particles" prompted Debra Houry, the CDC's then-chief medical officer, to send information to "help him with his talking points," according to an email she sent to senior CDC officials on May 1, 2025.

"Even though fetal cells are used to grow vaccine viruses, vaccines do not contain these cells or pieces of DNA that are recognizable as human DNA," she wrote to then-CDC chief of staff Matt Buzzelli and others. "Vaccines also do not contain fetal cells," she added.

Kennedy's statements stood in contrast to how prior health officials messaged around vaccinations by imploring Americans to get vaccinated, including during President Donald Trump's first term. Then-Health Secretary Alex Azar said communities had been the subject of "mass disinformation campaigns. … They need to get their kids vaccinated."

Public health experts say controlling outbreaks requires clear, repeated messages about vaccination, while acknowledging that declining trust in the CDC since the coronavirus pandemic has made federal officials less effective messengers. The CDC has not held a news briefing for reporters since Jan. 20, when the then-principal deputy director, Ralph Abraham, was asked whether losing elimination status would be significant and replied: "Not really. … You know, it's just the cost of doing business."

The health department has maintained that Kennedy has "repeatedly stated that MMR vaccination is the most effective way to prevent measles infection" and that "any notion that the Trump Administration is discouraging measles vaccination is absolutely fake news." Two doses of the shot provide 97 percent protection against measles.

Over the last year, dozens of measles outbreaks have taken hold across the country, and nationwide case counts have continued to climb. In West Texas, there were 762 cases during the 2025 outbreak. In South Carolina, the outbreak totaled 997 before it was declared over in April. And in Pennsylvania, officials have recorded 1,631 cases, including eight deaths, as of Friday.

In July, the U.S. reported the most measles cases in 35 years, surpassing last year's record total.

The resurgence, now totaling more than 5,800 cases nationwide, is posing myriad challenges for doctors and state health officials. Vaccine uptake has been declining for years amid rising skepticism. Meanwhile, outbreaks in traditionally undervaccinated communities are becoming harder to quickly extinguish.

Many doctors have never seen cases of measles, prompting health departments to educate clinicians on the basics and hospitals to quickly craft new protocols to safely isolate patients with a virus that can remain suspended in the air for up to two hours.

"Some of these outbreaks we've been seeing recently, for example, in Pennsylvania, it's not just kids who are getting sick," said Adriane Casalotti, who heads government and public affairs for the National Association of County and City Health Officials. "In fact, there's many more adults who are contracting measles, and that shows a longer pattern of undervaccination."

When immunizations in the broader population are high, it's easier to protect communities with lower vaccination rates. But that's not necessarily the case anymore, Casalotti said.

Pennsylvania has the largest measles outbreak in the country. But it's also been the center of a bitter political feud between Kennedy and Gov. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat widely viewed as a presidential contender.

When Pennsylvania reported its first two measles-associated deaths in 35 years in August, Kennedy suggested the deaths "may even have been altogether fabricated," and he accused Shapiro of using the moment for political gain. It wasn't the first time Kennedy had disputed the official state account of deaths; he questioned whether measles caused the death of one of the two Texas children who died during the 2025 outbreak.

Houry said such statements by Kennedy can leave the public with the impression that "maybe the disease isn't that deadly or that serious."

The CDC's Schwartz made the unusual decision to exclude those first deaths from the national tally, departing from the agency's practice of relying on state health departments to make those determinations. The agency has since added some deaths from Pennsylvania and says it is working with outside partners to craft a new definition of deaths due to measles.

The gap between federal and state counts has persisted as the toll has grown: States have now reported at least 11 measles-associated deaths this year in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York. The CDC's tally is six.

Kennedy's allies argue he should not be blamed for the rising cases of measles in the U.S., pointing to a worldwide resurgence and vaccine uptake that declined amid the covid pandemic.

Other countries have lost their elimination status and regained it after years of work. Venezuela lost its status in 2018 and regained it in 2023. Brazil regained its designation in November 2024, about five years after losing it.

Canada, which lost its status last year, has since stopped the continuous spread that cost it the designation, PAHO officials said. But it must go at least 12 months without measles spreading continuously before it can regain its status.

State and local health officials say regaining elimination status will require a national strategy that accounts for widely varying conditions on the ground. States with large ongoing outbreaks, such as Pennsylvania, require a different response from places that have kept high vaccination rates and are trying to prevent the virus from gaining a foothold.

In some communities where outbreaks are occurring, such as areas with Amish and Mennonite populations, some parents aren't necessarily opposed to vaccination or hesitant, but they don't get their children vaccinated because they don't routinely seek medical care.

Yet some public health experts fear the rhetoric in the second Trump administration could dissuade parents from getting their children vaccinated. Kennedy's approach to vaccines is part of a broader push within the Trump administration to reduce and space out the shots children receive.

While the administration has continued to recommend the MMR vaccine, Trump has suggested the combination vaccine could be "lethal," while acknowledging that he had no scientific evidence for the claim. He has said the vaccine should be broken up into three disease-specific shots, which medical groups say would offer no health benefit and could leave children vulnerable to more diseases for longer.

The changes have been embraced by some activists in the MAHA movement that helped propel Kennedy into office even as major medical organizations have condemned them. That creates a difficult dynamic as Kennedy tries to regain a public health designation that depends heavily on increasing vaccination, public health experts say.

The U.S. eliminated continuous measles transmission in 2000 through a combination of federal and state efforts, said Daniel Edney, president of the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials. States imposed vaccination requirements for schools, and the federal government created the Vaccines for Children program, which provides vaccines to about half the children in the U.S.

"Everybody was pulling together the same way," Edney said. "There was no dissension. The medical community was in alignment with public health, who was in alignment with the CDC … and everybody was working toward the same goal."

Caitlin Gilbert contributed to this report.

articles.title: 'Country's character remains the same': PM Modi praises people for heeding call to not buy gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday praised the people of India for heeding his appeal to avoid buying gold unless necessary for a year,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday praised the people of India for heeding his appeal to avoid buying gold unless necessary for a year, saying that their restraint led to a fall in gold prices.Addressing the 5th National Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh (Skill Convocation Ceremony) in Lucknow, PM Modi drew a parallel with former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri's appeal to citizens to give up one meal a day, saying that "the character of my country remains the same even today"."A year ago, I had appealed to the people of the country that if it was not necessary, they should refrain from buying gold for a year. I am happy that just as the people of this country had heeded Lal Bahadur Shastri ji's appeal to give up one meal a day, the character of my country remains the same even today," PM Modi said."When an ordinary person like me asked people not to buy gold, the people of the country bought less gold and its prices crashed. Today, people are telling me, 'Modiji, we listened to you and saved our money'," he added.The remarks came after PM Modi appealed to people to reduce fuel and gold consumption during public rallies, amid concerns over the US-Iran war and rising energy costs.Speaking at the convocation ceremony, PM Modi also said that people with practical skills would increasingly be valued more than those with formal educational certificates in the future."Today, I want to say one more thing. Mark my words, times are changing. Skilled people will be valued more than those who carry paper certificates and wear coats, trousers and ties," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Arizona parents wanted to replace a backyard gate so their disabled son could park his golf cart at home, but their HOA refused; an appeals court has rejected the association's attempt to force private arbitration
articles.summary: An Arizona couple who wanted to replace a backyard gate so their disabled son could park his golf cart at home have won a legal fight against their
articles.body: An Arizona couple who wanted to replace a backyard gate so their disabled son could park his golf cart at home have won a legal fight against their homeowners' association (HOA). An appeals court turned down the association's effort to force the family into private arbitration, allowing their lawsuit to move forward in court. Kevin and Jennifer LoPresto had asked the Wigwam Creek South Community Association to let them swap their single gate for a wider double gate. They explained that the wider opening was needed so their disabled son could park his golf cart in the backyard. The association denied their request and later argued that the dispute had to be settled through private arbitration instead of a public court.However, the Arizona Court of Appeals backed the lower court's refusal to order arbitration. In its September 25, 2026, memorandum decision, the court ruled that the arbitration rules used by the association were one-sided and could not be enforced against the couple. This ruling means the LoPrestos can keep fighting their case against the HOA in court. The appeals judges also granted the couple reasonable legal fees and court costs tied to the appeal. According to the decision posted by Justia, the case focuses on the association's rules, the couple's request to change their gate, and whether the HOA could force residents to settle disagreements through a private arbitration process.Request to replace backyard gate rejectedKevin and Jennifer LoPresto live in the planned neighborhood of Wigwam Creek South in Arizona. The community is run by the Wigwam Creek South Community Association and follows a set of rules called the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions. These rules control how properties in the neighborhood can be used and what changes homeowners can make to their houses and yards.In November 2024, the couple sent in a formal request to replace their single gate with a double gate. According to the court's decision, the goal was to allow "their disabled son [could] park his golf cart in the backyard." The association turned down the application. The LoPrestos challenged that choice, but the HOA stood by its refusal after reviewing their complaint.That disagreement eventually pushed the couple to go to court. In April 2025, Kevin and Jennifer filed a lawsuit against the association. They accused the HOA of breaking its contract duties and failing to act fairly when handling requests from homeowners. Their lawsuit argued that the HOA failed to follow the community's main rules, especially the duty to "enforce the rules and regulations . . . fairly, impartially, and without selective enforcement." The couple's court case centered on how the association handled their request and its duties under the neighborhood's governing rules.HOA wanted dispute settled through arbitrationInstead of letting the lawsuit move forward in court, the Wigwam Creek South Community Association asked the trial judge to send the fight to private arbitration. The association pointed to arbitration rules written in two documents. These were the community's Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions and a second rulebook called the Wigwam Creek South Community Association Guidelines for Community Living. The HOA claimed these rules forced the LoPrestos to settle their complaints through arbitration. It argued that the rules applied to the couple's claims and had to be followed.Arbitration is a process where a disagreement is settled outside the regular court system by an independent person or panel. People often use it to resolve contract fights without holding a full court trial. The association asked the Superior Court to force the couple to go through this process. The trial judge said no. The HOA then asked the court to clarify and rethink that choice, but the judge did not change the refusal to order arbitration. The association then appealed to the Arizona Court of Appeals, claiming the lower court had made an error.Appeals court finds arbitration rules one-sidedThe appeals court looked closely at both arbitration rules and decided that neither one could be enforced against the LoPrestos. In its ruling, the court noted that Arizona law generally supports written arbitration agreements as a way to settle fights quickly and for less money. Still, an agreement must meet basic fairness standards to hold up in court. The judges pointed to an earlier Arizona case, Stevens/Leinweber/Sullens, Inc. v. Holm Development and Management, Inc., which established that a one-sided arbitration rule can be considered substantively unconscionable. In plain terms, this means an agreement can be legally unfair because it puts strict rules on one side without placing similar duties on the other side.The court decided that the arbitration rule in the community's main declaration was one-sided. Under subsection 12.8.2, homeowners and other people covered by the declaration had to take their claims to arbitration. Yet subsection 12.8.1(a) excused the homeowners' association from that exact same requirement. The judges also pointed out that subsection 4.2 allowed the HOA to go to court to force residents to follow the declaration. This setup meant homeowners could be forced into private arbitration when suing the association, while the association kept the freedom to take disputes to court. The appeals court agreed that the lower court was right to call the rule unfair and unenforceable.Separate community guidelines also rejectedThe HOA also tried to use a second arbitration rule written in its Guidelines for Community Living. It argued that Section V of the guidelines was a separate, more specific rule that covered the LoPrestos' complaint. According to the association, this rule stayed valid even if the arbitration clause in the main declaration could not be used. The lower court had earlier questioned whether Section V had been properly approved as part of the original rules voted on by homeowners. It also questioned whether that rule matched the arbitration terms in the main declaration.The appeals court said it did not even need to answer those questions. Instead, the judges read the exact words of Section V and spotted another flaw. That rule applied when "any Owner has a dispute" with the HOA. The court noted that this wording only forced homeowners to take their fights to binding arbitration. It did not place that same duty on the association when the HOA took legal action against a homeowner. Because of this, the judges ruled that Section V was also one-sided. For the exact same reason as the arbitration rule in the main declaration, it was found to be unfair and unenforceable. The court turned down the association's appeal and backed the lower court's refusal to send the fight to arbitration.Couple awarded legal costsThe appeals court also reviewed the LoPrestos' request to get back the legal money they spent defending the lower court's ruling. The couple asked for attorneys' fees and court costs under sections 12-341.01 and 12-342 of Arizona law. The judges agreed to grant them reasonable legal fees and taxable costs for the appeal. They explained that the fight grew out of a contract dispute and the LoPrestos had successfully defended the lower court's ruling. This money award depends on the couple following the proper filing steps under Arizona Rule of Civil Appellate Procedure 21.The September 25, 2026, ruling came from the Arizona Court of Appeals, Division One. Presiding Judge Jennifer M. Perkins wrote the decision, and Judges Brian Y. Furuya and D. Andrew Gaona agreed with her. The ruling is an unpublished memorandum decision and is not precedential under Arizona Supreme Court Rule 111(c), which means it generally cannot be cited as binding law in future cases. The appeals court upheld the lower court's decision, leaving the LoPrestos free to pursue their original lawsuit against the Wigwam Creek South Community Association without being forced into private arbitration. This ruling does not decide whether the HOA must allow the double gate or settle the couple's main complaints. Those questions remain separate from the arbitration fight.You use AI every day. articles.title: Dream for president, nightmare for US Navy: Trump-class battleships add $275 billion to bill
articles.summary: Donald Trump's ambitious plan to build a new fleet of nuclear-powered battleships is turning into a costly burden for an already overstretched US Navy.
articles.body: Donald Trump's ambitious plan to build a new fleet of nuclear-powered battleships is turning into a costly burden for an already overstretched US Navy.With a new assessment warning that the proposed expansion could push annual shipbuilding costs far beyond the navy's own projections. The plan to acquire 15 Trump-class battleships is expected to add billions of dollars to an already massive naval expansion bill, raising questions over how Washington will fund its growing maritime ambitions while struggling to maintain its existing fleet.According to a report by the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) released on November 19, the US Navy's 30-year shipbuilding plan, covering 2027 to 2056, is expected to cost an average of $53.8 billion annually.This is around 18 per cent higher than the navy's own estimate of $45.7 billion a year. The CBO also projected that the Navy's annual shipbuilding expenditure would be 41 per cent higher than the average amount allocated over the previous five years, highlighting the growing financial demands of its fleet expansion programme.Under its ambitious expansion plan, the US Navy aims to increase its battle force fleet from 286 ships in 2026 to 398 by 2056.The plan involves purchasing 371 new battle force ships over the next 30 years, including seven aircraft carriers, 38 Virginia-class attack submarines, 16 next-generation SSN(X) submarines, 57 destroyers, 79 frigates and 15 Trump-class battleships. The Navy also plans to acquire 72 medium unmanned surface vessels as part of its future fleet.However, the proposed Trump-class battleships are emerging as one of the biggest cost drivers of the expansion. The CBO estimates that acquiring 15 such vessels could cost around $275 billion, significantly higher than the Navy's projection of $157 billion.This puts the estimated cost per battleship at approximately $18.3 billion, compared with the Navy's estimate of $10.4 billion. The $118 billion gap highlights the scale of the financial burden the programme could place on the Navy's long-term shipbuilding budget.The CBO also flagged a strategic contradiction in the navy's approach, noting that the battleship programme runs counter to its stated objective of distributing firepower across a larger number of ships and unmanned vessels.Instead, the proposed fleet would concentrate enormous firepower in a relatively small number of expensive warships, potentially increasing the risks associated with losing or disabling any one of them. The report further warned that the Navy's overall firepower could decline until 2035 as older missile-capable vessels are retired faster than new ones enter service.The financial burden comes at a time when the US Navy is already facing mounting operational pressure from the ongoing Iran war.According to a report by The Guardian, American warships have been deployed for extended periods, with some vessels spending more than 300 days at sea. Deployments have stretched to 10-11 months, well beyond the standard seven-month cycle, forcing the navy to postpone maintenance and repair work to keep its vessels operational.The prolonged deployments have also raised concerns over the strain on naval personnel and the readiness of the fleet.The Guardian reported that the USS Abraham Lincoln spent 265 days at sea without a port visit, while the return of USS George Washington from the Middle East ended a rare three-month period in which no US aircraft carrier was deployed across the Pacific.The extended operational commitments have added to concerns over whether the avy can sustain its global presence while managing an ambitious fleet expansion.

articles.summary: HARIDWAR: An Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer narrowly escaped serious injury after his temporary driver allegedly opened fire at him with a country-made
articles.body: HARIDWAR: An Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer narrowly escaped serious injury after his temporary driver allegedly opened fire at him with a country-made pistol inside his office in Kankhal on Saturday.The accused, Vinod Negi, was arrested and the weapon used in the attack recovered, police said.The bullet passed close to SP CP Nautiyal’s forehead. He was rushed to a nearby hospital before being referred to AIIMS Rishikesh."The SP’s condition was stable and he was out of danger," Haridwar SSP Navneet Singh Bhullar said.Bhullar said Negi was employed as a temporary driver. Police are probing a reported dispute between the accused and the officer, though the motive behind the alleged shooting has not yet been established.Preliminary inquiries have not revealed any criminal record against Negi, police said. articles.title: In 2026, Thailand installed 47 Hanuman-themed figures among 73 reef structures off Racha Yai; a monsoon later damaged part of the site and prompted a warning to divers
articles.summary: Discover the unique Hanuman-themed underwater installation off Koh Racha Yai, Thailand, which aims to promote marine conservation amidst challenges from seasonal monsoon currents.
articles.body: At Siam Bay, off Koh Racha Yai in Phuket, Thailand, in April 2026, an unusual underwater installation was completed. The project placed 73 structures on the seabed, which included 47 sculptures depicting Hanuman, the Hindu deity and one of the central characters of the Ramayana. The structure was designed to function as an artificial reef as well as an underwater attraction. The intention behind this installation was to provide surfaces for coral growth and create additional habitat for the marine ecosystem. However, within weeks of its installation, strong currents and underwater waves during a southwest monsoon damaged part of the structure. The authorities warned divers and diving operators to avoid the site because sections of the structure were unstable and were at risk of further collapse.An underwater reef inspired by the Hindu epic RamayanaKnown as Hanuman Nimitkai, the installation was developed under the initiative of The Magical Save Underwater World. According to the DMCR, between April 7 and 10, the transportation of the structures to the offshore location took place. Meanwhile, the underwater positioning and installation reportedly began on April 11. The 73 elements consisted of 47 Hanuman-themed sculptures, 15 three-dimensional-printed fence structures and 11 artificial coral reef units.At an approximate depth of 12 to 19 metres in Siam Bay, the structures were placed. The project’s objective was to combine marine conservation with sustainable tourism. The organisers intended the structures to provide a hard surface where coral larvae could attach and grow. This would eventually create a habitat for fish and other marine animals. In addition, the Hanuman installation was intended to become the first major attraction in a larger underwater art project. Later reports from The Phuket News noted that the wider aim of the project was to install sculptures depicting characters and episodes from the Ramayana. Therefore, the April installation represented an initial phase rather than the completion of the entire proposed underwater museum.Monsoon currents damaged part of the installationThe major setback came within a few weeks after the completion of the installation. On May 16, the authorities instructed diving shops, individual divers and instructors not to approach the Hanuman sculpture site until further notice. A report published by The Phuket News on May 19 noted that the right side of the structure had suffered severe damage. Strong currents and underwater waves during the southwest monsoon had reportedly caused significant movement in the rest of the sections, thus making them unstable and raising questions about safety.By September, officials had reported that the damaged Hanuman sculptures had been removed for repairs and had been reinstalled subsequently. The director of the Racha Islands Protected Area Management Center in Phuket told The Phuket News that the repairs had been completed, and that the sculptures had been open to visitors since August.Following the repairs, the wider project continued to advance. In September, reports described plans for additional sculptures depicting figures including Rama and Ravana. The plans also included installing scenes from the Ramayana. The underwater installation is reportedly scheduled for 2027. Therefore, the damage to the original Hanuman installation pointed out a practical challenge for the artificial reef project: structures placed underwater must be prepared in such a way that they can withstand seasonal changes in currents and wave conditions while remaining safe for divers and marine life.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'His visa wasn't immediately renewed': Prince Harry's reported US immigration trouble behind UK move; is it resolved now?
articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's decision to move back to the United Kingdom after spending nearly six years in California may have been prompted by an
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's decision to move back to the United Kingdom after spending nearly six years in California may have been prompted by an unexpected immigration issue involving the Duke of Sussex's US visa, according to a new report. The couple's return to Britain earlier this year had surprised royal watchers, with questions surrounding what prompted them to leave their Montecito home and relocate across the Atlantic with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. It was probably not homesickness, nor an attempt to mend things with the family, but possibly a visa bottleneck. A report by Page Six claimed that Harry encountered problems renewing his US visa before the family's departure. "His visa expired and wasn't immediately renewed," a US government source told Page Six.Another source reportedly backed the account. However, Harry's exact US immigration status has never been publicly disclosed, and neither he nor Meghan has confirmed that visa complications prompted their relocation.What kind of US visa did Prince Harry have?Harry's immigration status in the US has attracted attention since the publication of his memoir Spare, in which he disclosed past drug use. A lawyer cited by Page Six suggested that Harry could have held either a diplomatic visa or a visa issued to individuals with extraordinary ability or achievement. Both categories have renewal requirements, although the exact visa Harry held remains unknown.A former State Department official reportedly told Page Six that visa expiry and renewal requirements could explain the Sussexes' sudden departure from the US.Harry's immigration records became the subject of a legal dispute after the conservative Heritage Foundation questioned whether he had disclosed his past drug use in his US visa application. The Heritage Foundation challenged the US government's decision to grant him a visa, arguing that his disclosures raised questions about whether he had accurately answered questions on his immigration application. The conservative think tank sought access to his immigration records through a lawsuit. The dispute attracted attention because US visa applicants can face restrictions if they admit to certain past drug use.In 2024, the think tank lost the lawsuit against the DHS as US District Judge Carl Nichols ruled that Prince Harry's privacy interests outweighed any public interest in disclosing his visa records.Harry and Meghan reportedly planning US return for ChristmasDespite the reported visa complications, Harry's immigration issue appears to have been resolved as the couple are reportedly planning to travel back to California with Archie and Lilibet to spend Christmas with Meghan's mother, Doria Ragland.The Sussexes have spent recent months attending engagements in Britain and appear to have settled into their new life.Harry recently spoke about how his children were adjusting to their new surroundings during an appearance on British television programme This Morning. "It's a big culture shift," he said, referring to the children's transition to wearing school uniforms. He added that their confidence had improved considerably since joining a British school. "The confidence in both of them has gone through the roof since being at a UK school, which is really, really nice," he said.The US State Department explains that a visa's expiry date does not determine how long someone can legally remain in the country. That period is generally determined by the admission record, known as Form I-94. articles.title: Trump Admin moves to drop Alaska senate lawsuit after Peltola's victory
articles.summary: The Trump administration has dropped its legal challenge to the certification of Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska's US Senate race, allowing the Democrat to focus on her duties as the state's representative.
articles.body: The Trump administration has moved to abandon its legal challenge against the certification of Democrat Mary Peltola's victory in Alaska's US Senate race, after she secured enough votes to defeat Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.The US Department of Justice (DOJ) asked the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals on Thursday to declare the case moot, acknowledging that the election results had made its proposed investigation into possible voter confusion unworkable. The filing came two days after Peltola's victory was called, AP reportedThe lawsuit, filed at President Donald Trump's direction, sought to prevent Alaska officials from certifying Peltola as the winner until federal authorities could investigate whether voters had mistakenly supported another candidate with a name similar to Sullivan's.In its latest filing, DOJ attorneys asked the appeals court to overturn the lower court's decision dismissing the lawsuit, while also seeking to have the case dismissed because the election had concluded.The department said the court "should hold that this case is moot, vacate the underlying order, and remand for dismissal on that ground."The dispute centred on independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan, a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, Alaska, whose name appeared on the ballot alongside that of Republican Senator Dan S. Sullivan. The Alaska Supreme Court had previously ruled that the second candidate was legally entitled to contest the election.Peltola won an outright majority, becoming the Democrats' 56th senator and securing the party's ninth Senate pickup in the midterm elections. Her margin of victory was greater than the votes received by the second Sullivan.DOJ had argued that the presence of two candidates with similar names could have confused voters. However, the administration did not outline how investigators could establish whether ballots were mistakenly cast for one candidate rather than the other without compromising ballot secrecy.In its latest submission, the department acknowledged that the votes could no longer be individually identified after the election. Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said the government "reluctantly" accepted that there was no longer a way to establish whether votes for Daniel J. Sullivan were intended for the incumbent senator.Alaska's state government, which is controlled by Republicans, had also opposed the federal lawsuit. State attorneys described the legal challenge as "meritless" and filed documents supporting its dismissal.Peltola welcomed the administration's move, saying she wanted to focus on representing voters rather than continuing the legal dispute."Now that the election is over and the voters sent a very clear message about the direction they want our state to go in, I'm eager to move forward and get to work on behalf of all Alaskans," she said in a statement.The controversy surrounding the second Sullivan's candidacy intensified after The New York Times reported on text messages and other documents that appeared to indicate Peltola's campaign had been involved in recruiting him to enter the race. Sullivan has maintained that he ran independently, while Peltola has denied any involvement.Trump had also called for Peltola to be prosecuted over the alleged scheme. Federal investigators were sent to Alaska before election day as authorities examined whether the recruitment of the second Sullivan violated election laws. The Associated Press has reported that spoiler candidates with names resembling those of established politicians have featured in US elections for decades.The Justice Department's latest move marks at least the second time since the November 3 elections that the Trump administration has sought to withdraw a high-profile lawsuit concerning state election procedures.Earlier, the department moved to abandon a legal challenge targeting approximately 20,000 ballots in California. The administration had alleged that the ballots could belong to non-citizens, but state election officials disputed the reliability of the government's data, saying the list included US citizens.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Don't dislike BJP': Shehzad Poonawalla on quitting politics; calls rift with brother ideological
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former BJP spokesperson and Rise & Fall Season 2 winner Shehzad Poonawalla has said that his decision to quit active politics was not driven by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former BJP spokesperson and Rise & Fall Season 2 winner Shehzad Poonawalla has said that his decision to quit active politics was not driven by any dislike for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He also described his political differences with brother Tehseen Poonawalla as a "battle of principles" rather than a personal conflict.In an interview with news agency ANI, Shehzad reaffirmed his support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and Union home minister Amit Shah. He said he continued to hold the BJP in high regard and pointed to his choice of clothing as a sign of his association with the party."Why did I leave politics? It wasn't because I dislike the BJP; if I disliked them, I wouldn't be walking around wearing their T-shirt," he said.Speaking about his differences with his brother, Shehzad alleged that the issues raised by Tehseen were not in the nation's interest. He also claimed that his brother was aligned with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's team."I'm just glad these people weren't around during the time of the Mahabharata; otherwise, they would have claimed that the conflict between the Pandavas and the Kauravas was also just a publicity stunt! Our conflict isn't a personal one; it's a battle over principles. I feel that the issues he raises aren't actually in the nation's interest. In a way, it seems like he's part of Rahul Gandhi's team—much like how Arvind Kejriwal pushed Abhijeet Dipke to the forefront because his own credibility had hit zero," he said.He further contrasted his political loyalties with those of his brother, calling Tehseen a representative of the Congress and describing himself as an open supporter of the BJP's top leadership."Tehseen Poonawalla acts as 'Hamza Mazari' for the Congress. As for me, I'm an openly declared supporter of Modi, Yogi, and Amit Shah. For Uttar Pradesh, the combination of Modi and Yogi is only 'useful.' Yes, I have worked both with Rahul Gandhi and Modiji—and that's precisely why I can say, with my eyes closed, that this country won't see another Prime Minister like Modi-ji for the next 100 years," he said.Why Shehzad Poonawalla left active politicsExplaining his political journey, Shehzad said he had initially planned to remain with the BJP until the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. However, he continued working with the party through several subsequent state elections before deciding to return to the media."I left the Congress and joined the media, where I earned a very good salary as an anchor. Then, in 2021, I joined the BJP, with the intention of staying for about three to four years, until the 2024 elections. Then, there were crucial elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, and Bihar, and by the time those concluded, along with the Bengal elections, two years had passed; I moved on. After that, I decided to step away from politics and return to the media," he said.Shehzad also shared his views on Hindu identity and Hindutva, arguing that everyone living in India should identify as Hindu. He referred to the country as Bharat and Hindustan while explaining his position."Every person in this country is a Hindu, and everyone ought to be a 'Hindutva-vadi'. What else is this country called, besides Bharat? It is also known as Hindustan. And what does that imply? It means that anyone who lives here is a Hindu," he said.What Shehzad said about Rise & Fall Season 2 win\Reflecting on his victory in reality show Rise & Fall Season 2, Shehzad said winning the trophy was not his idea of a true political rise. He said he would consider it a bigger achievement if Yogi Adityanath secured another electoral victory in 2027 and Modi returned to power in 2029."Some might say that winning a trophy counts as a rise. For us, a true rise would be if Baba (Yogi Adityanath) wins the election for a third time in 2027, and if Modi-ji wins again in 2029... Shehzad Poonawalla might leave the BJP for financial cause, but the BJP can never truly leave Shehzad Poonawalla," he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US senate passes resolution honouring Fiona the hippo after Cincinnati Zoo star dies
articles.summary: The US Senate unanimously passed a resolution honoring Fiona, the beloved hippo from the Cincinnati Zoo, after her unexpected death due to complications from swallowing a hat. This article recounts her inspiring story and the heartfelt tributes that followed her passing.
articles.body: The GOP Senate has unanimously passed a resolution honouring Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippopotamus, a day after the animal died following complications from swallowing a visitor's hat that accidentally fell into her enclosure.Senator Bernie Moreno, a Republican from Ohio, announced the resolution on Friday, paying tribute to Fiona and recognising the zoo staff who cared for her throughout her life.Speaking on the Senate floor, Moreno described the hippo as a symbol of resilience and perseverance, saying her absence would be felt by the Cincinnati community and visitors who had travelled to see her."Fiona was a symbol of resilience, perseverance, and we're gonna miss her in Cincinnati," Moreno said.He added that her death would leave an emotional void for the zoo and the people who had followed her story. Moreno said the resolution was intended not only to recognise Fiona but also to acknowledge the efforts of the Cincinnati Zoo's leadership and staff, particularly those who looked after her every day.The zoo announced Fiona's death on Thursday after her condition deteriorated following the accidental ingestion of a knitted hat. The incident occurred around two weeks before her death, according to The People Although she initially showed no apparent signs of illness, her appetite subsequently declined, prompting veterinary staff to begin treatment.According to the zoo, its veterinary team conducted ultrasounds, administered fluids and medication, and consulted specialists while trying to help Fiona pass the object. Surgery was not considered an option because of her size and the medical risks involved. Despite continuous monitoring and several medical interventions, her condition did not improve.Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said the staff were struggling to process the loss and had not anticipated the outcome."We are in shock at the moment," Jenike said in a statement announcing her death. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."Fiona's death marked the end of a story that had attracted attention far beyond Cincinnati. Born prematurely in January 2017, she weighed just 29 pounds and needed intensive care because she could neither stand nor nurse independently. Zoo employees helped her through those early difficulties, and she eventually learned to do both, according to the outlet.Her progress turned her into one of the Cincinnati Zoo's best-known residents, with millions of people following her development and recovery. She is survived by her mother, Bibi, and her brother, Fritz.Following the announcement of her death, tributes poured in from supporters across the United States and other parts of the world. Jenike said the zoo had been moved by the public response, including displays of purple lighting at stadiums, bridges and buildings in Fiona's memory."We have received so much love from our community and beyond," he said in a separate statement.Moreno also described the incident involving the hat as an accident and called Fiona's death a devastating loss for the zoo community.You use AI every day. articles.title: US man sentenced to life for murdering British woman he groomed online and lured to America
articles.summary: A Florida man has been sentenced to life in prison for the kidnapping and murder of Sonia Exelby, a British woman he groomed online. The case highlights issues of mental health exploitation and the dangers of online relationships.
articles.body: A 54-year-old man has been sentenced to life in prison after a Florida jury found him guilty of kidnapping and murdering a British woman he had groomed online and persuaded to travel from the UK to the United States.Dwain Hall was convicted on Friday of kidnapping and first-degree murder in connection with the death of 32-year-old Sonia Exelby, who lived in Southsea, Hampshire. Her body was discovered buried in Marion County, Florida, on October 17 last year five days after she was reported missing from her home, according to BBC.Prosecutors told the court in Ocala that Hall, who used the online alias Alpha Sadist, had manipulated Exelby over several years after meeting her on a fetish website that is no longer operational. They alleged that he exploited her mental health difficulties and lured her thousands of miles away from home before killing her.Assistant State Attorney Amy Berndt said Hall had targeted Exelby because of her vulnerabilities and used the relationship to fulfil his own interests."He targeted her because of her mental illness and he exploited her for his own sadistic pleasure," Berndt told jurors at the start of the trial on Tuesday.She said Exelby had travelled to the US in a vulnerable state and was unable to make rational decisions when she was isolated from her family."And when he finally got her alone, thousands of miles away from home, completely incapable of making any rational decisions, he stabbed her to death and buried her body," Berndt said.The prosecution also told the jury that Hall had demanded $4,000 (£3,000) from Exelby for carrying out her death, describing him as her "executioner,” as per the outlet. The court heard that Exelby had struggled with mental illness and had been seeking someone to kill her.Berndt said there were men willing to exploit that vulnerability, adding that Exelby had been "trying to find someone who would kill her".The jury was instructed that a person's consent could not be used as a defence against a first-degree murder charge. The court clarified that valid consent must be given knowingly, voluntarily and with an understanding of the circumstances. Coerced submission resulting from exploitation, threats or intimidation did not qualify.Hall showed little reaction as the unanimous verdict was delivered. He was subsequently sentenced to life imprisonment.Exelby's family spoke about the impact of her death after the verdict. Her sister, Gemma Isaj, who testified during the proceedings, said her sibling had been exploited because of her vulnerability."A vulnerable person was preyed upon. A beautiful soul was taken," Isaj said.She added that the family would continue to campaign for greater awareness of mental health issues in Exelby's memory. Isaj also said her sister had believed that speaking about her experiences could prevent other people from being harmed.Exelby's brother, Barry Wilton, directly addressed Hall following the conviction, accusing him of pretending to care for his sister while exploiting her vulnerabilities."You had her life in your hands. You had the opportunity to save her, but instead you preyed on her vulnerabilities and you took her from us," Wilton said.Exelby was reported missing on October 12. Police established that she had left the UK, prompting an investigation involving authorities in the United States.After her body was discovered, investigators traced Hall through an attempted transaction involving Exelby's credit card by a roadside assistance company he owned.The family also raised concerns about online platforms where vulnerable individuals could be exposed to exploitation. Isaj specifically referred to the website Motherless.com, saying her sister's case had drawn attention to the risks associated with such sites.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Historic’ ruling in France: 3 police officers jailed for racist assault on Michel Zecler
articles.summary: Three French police officers have been sentenced to between one and two years in prison for racially motivated violence against a Black music producer,
articles.body: Three French police officers have been sentenced to between one and two years in prison for racially motivated violence against a Black music producer, Michel Zecler, in a landmark ruling delivered by a Paris court. The verdict, issued late Friday, recognised the racist nature of the assault, which took place six years ago during the coronavirus pandemic and was captured on camera.Zecler's lawyer, Serge Money, welcomed the verdict as a “historic ruling”, saying it was the first time the racist nature of the violence had been formally recognised in the case.“What is very important is that the racist nature of the violence he suffered has been recognized," Money told France Info. “As a legal professional, one can only be satisfied. This is a first.”Money said Zecler had consistently maintained from the beginning of the proceedings that the officers racially abused him. However, the defendants gave accounts that were somewhat inconsistent."Ultimately, they were convicted of lying, as the falsification of written records was established,” he said.The lawyer added that the officers had apologised. He also said the ruling could set a precedent for other victims of police violence whose accounts had not been believed.“This ruling should set a precedent for all those who have not been believed," he said. “There has to be a first, a starting point. It is now up to the justice system to make use of this ruling. I have no doubt that everyone will recognize its significance. This is no small matter, particularly given that the investigating judges had initially dismissed the racist dimension of the case."What happened to Michel ZeclerThe assault took place in November 2020 in Paris's 17th arrondissement. The three officers had approached Zecler, a music producer, for allegedly not wearing a face mask during coronavirus restrictions.Videos of the incident, obtained by The Associated Press, showed the officers following Zecler into his music studio. They repeatedly punched him, struck him with a truncheon and used tear gas against him.Zecler told the AP after the incident that the officers had repeatedly hurled insults at him, including a strong racist slur. He suffered injuries to his head, forearms and legs.“I want to understand why I have been assaulted by people who were wearing a police uniform," Zecler told the AP at the time. "I want justice actually, because I believe in the justice of my country."The lawyer said the video evidence was crucial to the case. Without it, Zecler would have ended up in prison, he added.Zecler had initially been taken into custody on suspicion of violence against public authority.Fresh focus on police conductThe case has renewed attention on allegations of excessive force and racism within French law enforcement agencies, which have faced longstanding criticism over their treatment of minorities.Then-justice minister Eric Dupond-Moretti had said he was scandalised by the footage. He acknowledged that some police officers were racist but denied that racism was systemic within the force.Rap artist Stomy Bugsy also welcomed the verdict, calling it a victory for victims of police misconduct.“this is a victory for all victims. If it can help curb, reduce and ultimately put an end to this kind of police misconduct and abuse, then it is a victory.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: A cargo vessel heading towards Russia's Kaliningrad exclave was struck by two drones in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, raising fresh concerns over maritime security near Nato territory.According to Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko, the vessel was attacked in international waters, west of Russia's Gogland Island and around three nautical miles from the Russian maritime border.The ship, identified as Sparta II, caught fire following the attack and subsequently drifted into Finnish territorial waters.Finnish authorities responded to the incident, with the country's Border Guard monitoring the vessel and preparing for possible rescue and environmental protection operations.Sparta II is operated by Oboronlogistics, a company linked to Russia's defence ministry. The vessel has been under US sanctions since 2022 and has previously been associated with transporting military equipment, including S-300 air defence systems from Syria to Russia.Its links to Russia's military logistics network make the attack particularly significant. However, there is no confirmed information that the ship was carrying military equipment when it was struck.The attack took place in the Gulf of Finland, a strategically important maritime corridor connecting Russia's St Petersburg region to the wider Baltic Sea. The gulf is bordered by Russia, Finland and Estonia, both Finland and Estonia being members of Nato.The location is particularly sensitive because of its proximity to Nato territory and the importance of the Baltic Sea to Russian maritime operations. The incident also comes amid heightened tensions between Moscow and Nato countries following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.Finnish authorities said Ukraine was likely behind the attack, Reuters reported. However, Kyiv has not claimed responsibility for the strike, and the circumstances surrounding the attack remain under investigation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Bradford councillor Ibrar Ali was stabbed multiple times during community work. A suspect has been charged with attempted murder. Read more about the incident and Ali's condition.
articles.body: Bradford councillor Ibrar Ali was stabbed multiple times while intervening to protect a council staff member during community work in his ward, his family has said. The 32-year-old man accused of the attack has been charged with attempted murder.According to West Yorkshire Police, the councillor was attacked at around 11.04am on Thornbury Avenue before being taken to nearby Manse Street, BBC reported.In a statement, Ali's family said he had been carrying out street-cleaning work alongside Bradford Council employees when the incident occurred. They said he stepped in to protect a member of the council staff and sustained multiple stab wounds during the attack.The family confirmed that although his injuries were serious, they were not life-threatening."Alhamdulillah [praise be to God], although his injuries are serious, they are not life-threatening. He is currently receiving treatment in hospital and remains in a stable condition," the statement said.Police arrested a 32-year-old man following a stand-off lasting more than three hours on the roof of a property on Thornbury Avenue. The suspect, identified as Arfan Ali, of Thornbury Avenue, was subsequently charged with attempted murder, assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.He appeared before Leeds Magistrates' Court and was remanded in custody. He is due to appear at Bradford Crown Court on December 21.The councillor's family also acknowledged the assistance provided by emergency services and members of the public who responded to the incident. They thanked police officers, paramedics and those who provided first aid at the scene."The family would like to express their heartfelt gratitude to everyone who has offered prayers, kind words and messages of support during this difficult time," the statement added.They also asked people to remember Ali and his family in their duas, or prayers, as he continues to receive medical treatment.Ali represents Bradford Moor ward as a member of the Your Bradford Independent Group. articles.title: France moves to take Rohingya genocide row to UN security council after Myanmar rejects ICJ verdict
articles.summary: The Myanmar-Rohingya genocide row is showing no signs of dying down.
articles.body: The Myanmar-Rohingya genocide row is showing no signs of dying down. Days after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) delivered a landmark verdict holding Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya in 2017, the country has rejected the ruling, setting the stage for a fresh diplomatic confrontation.France is now stepping in, seeking to take the matter to the United Nations security council and push for action over Myanmar's refusal to comply with the court's verdict.According to news agency Reuters, France's foreign ministry said it would seek a meeting of the UN security council following Myanmar's rejection of the ICJ ruling.The ministry stressed that decisions delivered by the world court are final and binding on the parties involved and must be implemented in accordance with international law.France also pointed to the UN charter, which allows the Security Council to consider measures to enforce an ICJ judgment if a party to the dispute fails to comply with it.Under Article 94 of the UN charter, all member states are obligated to comply with decisions of the International Court of Justice in cases to which they are parties.Article 94(2) further provides that if a party fails to fulfil its obligations under a court judgment, the other party to the case may approach the UN security council.In this case, The Gambia, which brought the genocide case against Myanmar, can seek the council's intervention over its failure to comply with the ruling. The security council may then make recommendations or decide on measures to give effect to the judgment.There have been previous instances of countries approaching the UN Security Council over non-compliance with ICJ judgments. In 1986, Nicaragua sought the council's intervention after the United States refused to comply with an ICJ ruling that found Washington had violated international law through its military activities against Nicaragua.However, the US vetoed a draft resolution calling for compliance with the judgment, preventing further action.In another instance, Honduras approached the security council in 2002, seeking intervention to ensure implementation of a 1992 ICJ judgment settling a territorial and maritime dispute with El Salvador.However, the council did not make any recommendation to enforce the ruling. These cases highlight the difficulties of securing compliance with ICJ judgments through the security council, particularly when permanent members exercise their veto powers.China and Russia, both permanent members of the council with veto powers, have maintained close ties with Myanmar's military leadership. Any substantive resolution would require at least nine votes in favour and no veto from any of the five permanent members, meaning opposition from either Beijing or Moscow could block proposed action.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A luxury home in Florida has nearly doubled in value after selling for $13.25 million, setting a new residential property record in Glenvar Heights near
articles.body: A luxury home in Florida has nearly doubled in value after selling for $13.25 million, setting a new residential property record in Glenvar Heights near Miami. According to Mansion Global, local real estate records and reporting by Miami property specialists, the estate was owned by advertising executive Jose Dans Jr. and his wife, Heide Carina Dans, who purchased the land in 2024 before developing an expansive private residence. Dans, founder and president of the Coral Gables-based marketing agency Wow MKTG, bought the nearly one-acre property for $7.3 million. He and his wife subsequently built a 9,229-square-foot, Carolinas-inspired mansion, which they occupied for approximately 18 months before putting it on the market.The property was initially listed for $13.75 million in August 2026. It eventually sold for $13.25 million, with the transaction closing on November 13, according to local multiple listing service records cited by real estate professionals. The sale has established a new benchmark for Glenvar Heights, surpassing the previous residential record of $7.4 million set in December 2025. The transaction also places the neighbourhood among Miami-Dade County’s increasingly sought-after luxury residential markets.The estate features a five-bedroom main residence, a detached guesthouse and a separate cabana. Designed with an emphasis on entertaining and high-end living, the property combines extensive landscaping with contemporary technology and premium interior finishes.Among its standout features is a driveway constructed from Turkish basalt marble, which leads to the main entrance. Inside, the home has white oak flooring, bespoke woodwork and a kitchen fitted with a La Cornue Château range. The main residence includes five full bathrooms and two half bathrooms, while its automated systems incorporate a concealed sound system, exterior laser security alarms, a generator and a water-softening installation.The additional structures provide further accommodation and entertainment space. The detached guesthouse has one bedroom and one bathroom, while the cabana includes its own bathroom and an air-conditioned summer kitchen. Outside, the grounds feature an oversized heated swimming pool and an outdoor kitchen equipped with Sub-Zero and Wolf appliances.Parking facilities include a two-car garage with an electric vehicle charging system, a three-car carport and additional space for five vehicles. The property was designed to offer the experience of a private retreat while remaining connected to Miami’s commercial and entertainment districts. Glenvar Heights is approximately 10 miles southwest of downtown Miami and offers access to areas such as Coral Gables, Coconut Grove and the shopping destination Merrick Park.Listing agent Angel Nicolas of Serhant attributed the property’s appeal to its landscaping, construction quality and location. He also pointed to its accessibility to Miami International Airport as an important consideration for the eventual buyer.The identity of the new owners has not been publicly established. Compass agents Audrey Ross and Lisa Sayfie, who represented the buyers, had not responded to requests for comment at the time of Mansion Global’s report.For Dans, the sale is another addition to an established interest in residential property development. He and his wife have reportedly renovated and sold 14 other houses, approaching each project with an emphasis on premium materials and carefully designed living spaces. articles.title: A New York couple have donated 77 acres of wooded land feeding a town's drinking-water reservoir, permanently blocking development that could threaten the water supply while allowing residents to hike there
articles.summary: “The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others,” Mahatma Gandhi once said.
articles.body: “The best way to find yourself is to lose yourself in the service of others,” Mahatma Gandhi once said. Generosity is often measured by what we give to others, but some acts of kindness go beyond an immediate gesture. They protect something that entire communities depend on, sometimes benefiting generations of people who may never even know who made it possible.We often hear stories of human greed around us, in newspapers, on TV and on social media. Sometimes, they almost make us wonder whether the world is still a liveable place. And in those moments, what we need is a piece of hay in the middle of the ocean, something to hold on to when everything around us seems overwhelming. One couple has done something that feels exactly like that.In New York, Jerry and Joanne Braun have donated approximately 77 acres of land to the Town of Newburgh, ensuring that it remains protected from future development. The property is particularly important because the streams and tributaries that pass through it feed into the Chadwick Lake Reservoir, a vital source of drinking water for the town. articles.summary: First Lady Melania Trump has expressed hope that Russia and Ukraine could agree to another ceasefire before Christmas, saying she wants to see more pauses
articles.body: First Lady Melania Trump has expressed hope that Russia and Ukraine could agree to another ceasefire before Christmas, saying she wants to see more pauses in fighting even as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of repeatedly rejecting proposals to de-escalate the war. Speaking to Fox News host Jesse Watters about her Christmas wish, Melania said she wanted world peace but specifically hoped for more ceasefires between the two countries."I would really like to have more ceasefire. We could do it very fast if both Ukraine and Russia are willing," she said.The first lady added that she was already involved in discussions and hoped another ceasefire could be secured before December 25.Her remarks come after she helped facilitate a six-day humanitarian ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky in the Kherson region last month. The temporary truce, which ran from October 27 to November 1, allowed humanitarian assistance to reach residents and nearly 800 people to be evacuated, according to the White House.Melania said she was involved in the planning of the operation, including discussions about demining, evacuation routes, hospital access, transportation and medical resources.She has described the Oleshky agreement as a possible starting point for broader cooperation between Moscow and Kyiv.Zelenskyy thanks Melania for Oleshky, sends list of 15 Ukrainian settlements for similar ceasefireUkrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has indicated that Melania Trump's humanitarian initiative in Oleshky could be replicated in other Russian-occupied settlements, as Kyiv prepares for further evacuation operations.In a statement shared on X, Zelenskyy thanked the US first lady for her role in helping unblock the situation in Oleshky and evacuate Ukrainian civilians."We are grateful to the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump, for Oleshky, for helping unblock and evacuate our people," he said. Zelenskyy said he had discussed the possibility of conducting similar humanitarian operations with Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Mykhailo Drapatyi. They had reviewed the number of people who could potentially be evacuated and the work already completed. The Ukrainian president said an updated list of settlements had been approved and shared with Ukraine's Ombudsman and the US side.The proposed locations include nine settlements in the Kherson region and six in the Zaporizhzhia region.Settlements identified in the Kherson region:- Radensk- Kostohryzove- Hola Prystan- Stara Zburivka- Nova Zburivka- Hladkivka- Velyki Kopani- Kardashynka- Velyka KardashynkaSettlements identified in the Zaporizhzhia region:- Mayachka- Zlatopil- Dniprorudne- Kamyanske- Verkhnia Krynytsia- VasylivkaZelenskyy stressed that the list would be updated, suggesting that Kyiv is considering expanding the humanitarian evacuation effort to additional locations.Senior advisor to Melania Trump, Marc Beckman, called the First Lady a 'peace leader'' and said she was the first First Lady to ever go in front of the United Nations Security Council and deliver her wise speech about peace through education.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2020, Dua Lipa bought a £6.75 million Victorian home in London; six years later, it is still being rebuilt with a basement pool, cinema and studio, with completion now expected in 2027
articles.summary: Dua Lipa bought a £6.75 million Victorian house in Hampstead in 2020, but six years later the property is still being rebuilt.
articles.body: Dua Lipa bought a £6.75 million Victorian house in Hampstead in 2020, but six years later the property is still being rebuilt. The singer’s ambitious renovation, which includes a basement pool, cinema, and music studio, is now expected to finish in 2027, according to The Standard and Geo News. The delay reflects the scale of the project rather than a lack of progress. After buying the Arts and Crafts style home at the start of 2020, Lipa submitted plans in 2021 for a major overhaul, but construction did not begin until 2024 after a long planning process. Read more about it, as per the reports, here:A home with big plansThe Hampstead property sits on one of the area’s most prized leafy avenues. Lipa bought the Victorian house for £6.75 million in early 2020 and shared glimpses of its interiors during the first Covid 19 lockdown, including a marbled bathroom and a large kitchen with sliding glass doors to the garden.Rather than making small updates, she chose a full transformation. The plans were drawn up by 4M Group, the architecture practice behind the first Kosovo Pavilion at the Venice Architecture Biennale in 2012.The design calls for three bedrooms across two upper floors, living spaces at ground level, a library and drawing room beside the entrance hall, and a large open plan area combining the kitchen, garden room, and dining space.The basement that changed everythingThe most ambitious part of the project is the basement extension. It will include a subterranean swimming pool beneath the back garden, along with a steam room, shower, and changing area.The basement will also contain a cinema and studio workspaces. The studio is intended to allow work activity to be separate from the rest of the house, giving Lipa a dedicated space for music and creative projects.Geo News reported that the renovation is expected to cost around £3 million. The combination of a pool, cinema, studio, and extensive below ground construction helps explain why the project has taken so long.A long planning battleThe project faced opposition from the Redington Frognal Neighbourhood Forum, which raised concerns about the impact on a local conservation area. Camden Council ultimately approved the plans in 2023.Basement excavations have been controversial in Camden, particularly in expensive neighbourhoods such as Hampstead. In 2017, several neighbourhood forums sought stronger planning rules after residents experienced subsidence, flooding, and construction disruption linked to basement developments.The approval came with conditions. The council required strict construction restrictions to ensure that noise from mechanical installations and equipment would not harm the amenity of people living nearby.Construction began only in 2024Although Lipa’s team first applied for permission in 2021, construction did not start until 2024. The three year wait was driven by the complexity of the plans and the need to address local concerns. Local groups worried about the loss of green space, the protection of old trees, and the possibility of flooding in the area. As a result, builders have had to work carefully while digging metres underground.Around 20 workers have reportedly been on site for more than a year. The team has also committed to keeping noise and dust to a minimum and to reducing disruption for nearby residents and businesses.Why the project takes so longDesign expert Leigh Ann Raines told Geo News that projects like this naturally take longer than usual because of their complexity. She noted that Lipa could be investing £3 million to create a home suited to her needs.A basement pool, cinema, and studio are not simple additions. They require structural work, waterproofing, ventilation, drainage, and careful coordination with the existing Victorian building. The need to protect nearby trees and manage construction in a conservation area adds another layer of difficulty. These constraints can slow progress, but they also reflect the care required when working in a historic London neighbourhood.What the finished home may look likeWhen complete, the house will combine traditional Victorian character with modern amenities. The upper floors will provide bedrooms, while the ground level will offer generous living, dining, and garden facing spaces. Below ground, the home will gain a level of privacy and functionality that few London properties can match. The pool, steam room, cinema, and studio will create a self contained entertainment and work zone beneath the garden.For Lipa, the finished home may finally offer the space to relax, create, and host without leaving Hampstead. For now, though, the singer will have to wait until 2027 before the project is complete.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
