articles.title: Alarms ring as military drone tenders specify China-linked parts, Indian industry cites security risk
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cautioning the govt against sourcing drones with Chinese components, the country’s industry body Drone Federation India (DFI) has told senior
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cautioning the govt against sourcing drones with Chinese components, the country’s industry body Drone Federation India (DFI) has told senior defence officials that as many as 689 tenders floated on govt e-Marketplace (GeM) by the Indian military and govt bodies over nearly six years were found to specify Chinese drones and drone components.DFI, which has over 1,000 firms as members and represents the collective voice of India’s drone and counter-drone ecosystem, on Friday submitted a formal representation to defence secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General N S Subramani, revealing public procurement tenders floated on GeM by military, security forces and govt agencies “specified Chinese-origin drones or drone components”.DFI reviewed GeM tenders from March 10, 2021 to Nov 19, 2026 and found out that “84% of these tenders (689) come from the Indian Army itself”. “580 of them raised by Indian Army units. Tenders asked for Chinese drones or drone parts. 355 tenders between Jan and Nov 19, 2026, almost double the 190 in all of 2025,” DFI said on Friday in a series of posts on X.Responding to DFI’s grievance, defence officials told TOI, “GeM is a neutral platform which connects a buyer and a seller. However, a buyer (such as Army units) doesn’t have the freedom to select a seller. A buyer can only give specifications what it wants. Based on specifications, sellers offer their products at the lowest cost and then there is a reverse auction among sellers for products of large values, which reinforce transparency of GeM. GeM also ensures that an item with the lowest price is made available to the buyer.”The officials further told TOI, “GeM doesn’t allow a buyer to select or favour any particular brand or product at any stage. At the Army’s level, there are checks and balances that are maintained to ensure that products meeting specifications are only purchased. If a seller is caught lying about the use of Chinese components in its item, it is liable to be blacklisted by the Army.”Giving details of China-linked brands, DFI in its post said, “DJI, RadioMaster, SpeedyBee, HGLRC, GEPRC, Skydroid, T-Motor, EMAX, RumCam, Caddx, Hobbywing, Holybro, Foxeer, iFlight, FlySky and SIYI. All 16 of the most-named brands are headquartered in China... DJI or RadioMaster appear in 450 of the 689 tenders.”Calling it a security risk, DFI said, “Once a tender names a Chinese part, the risk is already inside our system.” The industry body is pushing for no Chinese parts in drones or components bought by the Indian forces and for preference to be given to Indian components in every such buy, and wants the ‘country of origin’ to be declared in every bid.

articles.title: Mexico drug cartel leader's arrest sparks deadly violence in Sinaloa; 11 killed
articles.summary: A major military operation to capture one of the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives triggered a wave of violence in Mexico's northwestern Sinaloa state,
articles.body: A major military operation to capture one of the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives triggered a wave of violence in Mexico's northwestern Sinaloa state, leaving at least 11 people dead, authorities said on Saturday.Mexican security forces arrested alleged cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro', following an overnight gun battle with suspected cartel gunmen in the city of Guasave. The violence saw armed men set up roadblocks using burning vehicles, businesses and trucks set ablaze, and residents forced to take shelter as military helicopters and drones flew overhead, reported Associated Press.Mexico's Defense Cabinet said seven suspected cartel gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the gun battle during the operation which was carried out with assistance from US intelligence, according to the Mexican government.The violence also disrupted a baseball match in Guasave, where spectators fled the stadium as gunfire rang out. Videos circulating on social media showed people scrambling for cover, burning vehicles and military helicopters flying over the city.How the operation unfoldedMexico's Defence Ministry said elite military forces used "stealth and surprise" to establish a security perimeter around the building where Meza Flores was staying.However, suspected cartel operatives retaliated with gunfire and explosives as security forces moved in to arrest him. The group also established at least 10 roadblocks using burning vehicles, delaying the extraction of the arrested leader.Mexican forces were unable to take Meza Flores out of Guasave until around 4 am on Saturday, a federal official told The Associated Press. He was subsequently flown to Mexico City to appear before prosecutors.Local residents described scenes of widespread panic as the fighting spread across the city. Several businesses, including Oxxo convenience stores, were burned, while trucks continued to block roads on Saturday."The fighting was happening all over Guasave. It spread throughout the city," local journalist Alma Camacho told AP.Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said armed forces would remain deployed across Sinaloa to protect civilians.Read more: How Mexico hunted down FBI's most-wanted drug lord; watchWho is 'El Chapo Isidro'?Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known by the nickname 'El Chapo Isidro' is the alleged leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation, also known as Los Mazatlecos, a criminal group based in Guasave. He rose through the ranks of the Beltrán Leyva cartel before establishing his own organisation.He is among the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives, with the US agency offering a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.According to the FBI, Meza Flores was wanted for allegedly possessing, distributing and importing large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States. He was indicted in 2019 on drug trafficking and firearms charges and had also faced drug trafficking charges in 2012.The US Treasury Department had identified his organisation in 2013 as being involved in an extremely violent turf war with the rival Sinaloa Cartel, then led by Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán, who is now serving a prison sentence in the US.Meza Flores was also a key ally of 'Los Mayos', a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel that was designated a foreign terrorist organisation by the Trump administration last year.Meza Flores' arrest comes amid an ongoing power struggle between rival factions of the Sinaloa Cartel for control of the northern Mexican state.His organisation has been aligned with Los Mayos, which has been involved in a conflict with another faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. His capture could further intensify the struggle over territory, drug trafficking routes and control of criminal networks.Mexican security analyst David Saucedo warned that targeting senior cartel leaders without dismantling their wider organisations could trigger further violence.The strategy, often called the 'kingpin strategy', focuses on capturing or killing high-ranking cartel figures. However, experts have argued that removing leaders can create power vacuums, prompting rival factions and remaining members to fight for control."What is evident is this is a product of pressure from the United States," Saucedo said, adding that the arrest of senior figures does not necessarily dismantle the wider network of armed operatives, street-level dealers and political and police connections.The arrest also comes as US President Donald Trump has increased pressure on Mexico to crack down on drug cartels. The Mexican government said intelligence provided by the Trump administration helped authorities locate and capture Meza Flores, although it did not disclose details of the coordination.US and Mexican officials welcomed the arrest. US Ambassador Ronald Johnson said the operation demonstrated what cooperation between the two countries could achieve, while García Harfuch described the detention as "an important step in pacifying Sinaloa".However, analysts have cautioned that the capture of another high-profile cartel leader could set off fresh clashes in a region already grappling with factional violence.You use AI every day.
